headline: Crypto flat near $77,900 on a quiet Sunday; stocks reopen Monday
summary: Crypto is flat on Sunday afternoon: bitcoin sits near $77,900 (up 0.3% in 24 hours) and ether near $2,261 after Binance's withdrawal reopening went smoothly, while Lighter (LIT) and Pearl lead the large-coin gainers, each up about 7–8%. Stocks are closed after Friday's worst day since June (Nasdaq −2.9%, S&P 500 −1.8%, TSX −1.7%), and oil traders will react to Iran's conditional offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz when futures reopen Sunday evening. Next week is packed: Apple, Shopify and AMD earnings, the U.S. midterms on Tuesday and the U.S. jobs report on Friday.

crypto.label: Fearful
crypto.why: The Fear & Greed index reads 34 (Fear), up from 30 but below 51 earlier in the week; the whole crypto market is worth about $2.61 trillion, down about 3.5% in 24 hours as many smaller coins lag while bitcoin, now about 60% of the market, holds steady.

stocks.label: Risk-off
stocks.why: Chip and big-tech stocks led Friday's broad sell-off, the VIX fear gauge jumped 13% to 19.4, and markets are pricing a good chance of another Fed hike in December.

drivers.title: Big Tech's AI bills spook investors
drivers.detail: Alphabet fell 12.6% Thursday after missing profit estimates while spending over $51 billion in one quarter on capital projects, then Intel's weak outlook (down 28.6%) and Amazon's negative free cash flow hit chip stocks Friday. A chip-stock index fell more than 7% as investors questioned when AI spending will pay off.

drivers.title: Binance restarts withdrawals after record $6.3 billion hack
drivers.detail: Binance reopened withdrawals Sunday, starting with bitcoin and then selected coins on 14 other networks including Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Tron; it says about 95% of the stolen assets have been replaced from its own reserves, with roughly $3 billion, mostly stablecoins, frozen. Other coins wait on security checks with no set timeline, the FBI has tied the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor group, and a full proof-of-reserves check (a way for users to verify their coins are backed) is promised by Nov. 3.

drivers.title: Central banks lean toward hiking, not cutting
drivers.detail: The Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28 after a September hike, and futures priced roughly an 83% chance of a December increase, per Kitco. The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.50% the same day, its first hike in three years, and said more may be needed because of high energy prices.

drivers.title: Iran offers a conditional 48-hour Hormuz reopening
drivers.detail: Iran said overnight it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if Washington first grants sanctions relief, frees frozen funds, restores oil waivers and scales back its military presence; Trump said talks were going fine but the U.S. is 'not in a hurry.' U.S. crude closed Friday at $104.12, a six-month high, after a tanker was hit near the strait, so any real progress could pull oil and inflation fears lower, while a collapse of talks could push them higher.
drivers.assets: Oil, Canadian energy stocks, inflation, bond yields

drivers.title: Gold slides to a one-year low
drivers.detail: Gold futures fell 3.3% to about $3,899, as the prospect of higher interest rates and forced selling outweighed safe-haven demand. That dragged TSX materials stocks down 4.8% on Friday.

crypto.name: Bitcoin
crypto.move: Up 0.3% in 24h but down 3.4% this week, at about $77,900 (down 8.4% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitcoin hit about $81,900 on Thursday before the Binance hack news set off a wave of liquidations (forced selling of borrowed, leveraged bets), sending it to a six-week low near $76,300. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs (funds that hold real bitcoin and trade like stocks) saw about $643 million of outflows on Friday, ending four days of inflows. Binance reopened bitcoin withdrawals early Sunday and then other major networks, and the price has barely moved, holding near $78,000; analysts cited by crypto.news see $76,000–$77,000 as the key support zone.
crypto.meaning: The price held up better than you might expect after the largest crypto theft ever, which suggests the hack is being treated as a Binance problem rather than a flaw in bitcoin itself. But with ETF buyers retreating and rates possibly rising, there is little fresh demand to lift it quickly.

outlook.bullCase: A smooth restart of Binance withdrawals, a return to ETF inflows and a calm reaction to the U.S. midterms could take it back toward the $80,000–$82,000 range it hit on Thursday.
outlook.bearCase: If more stolen coins hit the market, ETF outflows continue or a hot jobs report cements a December Fed hike, a break below the ~$76,000 low could open the way to the low $70,000s.
outlook.watch: How smoothly Binance withdrawals run and when the next networks open; daily ETF flow figures; the $76,000 support and $82,000 resistance; U.S. midterms (Nov. 3) and jobs report (Nov. 6).

crypto.name: Ethereum
crypto.move: Up 0.2% in 24h but down 3.8% this week, at about $2,261 (down 15.8% over 30 days)
crypto.why: A large share of the stolen Binance funds was ether and stablecoins, and ether dropped more than 3% to a two-month low near $2,178 when the hack broke. Ether ETFs also had outflows of about $156 million on the same day bitcoin funds bled $643 million. Ethereum was in the first group of networks to reopen for Binance withdrawals on Sunday, and the price has steadied around $2,260.
crypto.meaning: Ether has fallen harder than bitcoin over the past month, a sign that investors are favouring the biggest, most liquid coin when nervous. A holder should expect bigger swings than bitcoin in either direction.

outlook.bullCase: If the hacker's ether stays frozen or tracked and risk appetite returns, a move back above $2,400 is possible.
outlook.bearCase: Selling of stolen ether through decentralized exchanges or continued ETF outflows could push it below the $2,178 low toward $2,000.
outlook.watch: On-chain movement of the hacker's wallets; ether ETF flows; whether $2,178 holds.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist

crypto.name: TRON
crypto.move: Up 1.9% in 24h but down 4.9% this week, at about $0.3133 (down 6.7% over 30 days)
crypto.why: TRON had climbed above $0.36 right after the Binance hack, but blockchain firm TRM Labs says much of that buying came from the attackers themselves: they moved about $628 million through the TRON network and swapped roughly $234 million of the stablecoin USDT into TRX before Tether froze the linked wallets. With that artificial demand gone, the price has fallen back and given up the whole spike. Derivatives traders are also leaning bearish, with funding rates (the fee between long and short traders) negative.
crypto.meaning: The earlier jump was not a sign of real new demand, so holders should not read it as a breakout. TRON's core business, moving USDT payments, is unchanged, but the coin may stay volatile while hacker-linked TRX is still in circulation.

outlook.bullCase: If the hacker-linked TRX is frozen or stops moving and the wider market recovers, it could climb back to $0.33–$0.34.
outlook.bearCase: If the attackers dump their TRX or crypto keeps sliding, a break below $0.31 could open the way to about $0.30.
outlook.watch: On-chain movement of hacker-linked TRX wallets; the $0.31 support and $0.33 resistance; funding rates on TRX futures.

sources.title: CoinTurk: Tron falls 6% as Binance hackers move $628M through network
Coinpaper: TRX drops 6% as Binance hack fallout reverses rally

crypto.name: Hyperliquid
crypto.move: Down 0.6% in 24h but up 13.6% this week, at about $87.56 (down 1.4% over 30 days)
crypto.why: HYPE jumped about 15% on Thursday after Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, agreed to work with TradeXYZ to offer Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures (contracts with no expiry date) to U.S. traders, pending regulatory approval. The token has held most of that gain, near $88. A modeled release of roughly 9.9 million HYPE (about $920 million) to core contributors is expected around Nov. 6.
crypto.meaning: The ICE deal is a big vote of confidence from traditional finance, but it still needs approval and has no launch date. The large scheduled unlock could add selling pressure in the short term.

outlook.bullCase: Regulatory progress on the ICE plan or a quiet unlock could send it back toward the ~$98 record high.
outlook.bearCase: Heavy selling around the Nov. 6 unlock or a weaker crypto market could push it back below $80.
outlook.watch: Nov. 6 contributor unlock; any CFTC news on the ICE–TradeXYZ venue; the $98 high.

sources.title: The Block: HYPE surges as ICE moves to bring Hyperliquid perps to U.S.

crypto.name: Aave
crypto.move: Up 0.1% in 24h and down 1.7% this week, at about $135.02 (down 26.0% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Aave, the biggest crypto lending protocol, froze markets across 16 networks after a wallet linked to the Binance hacker started borrowing against stolen funds, then reopened them with nine assets still blocked from being used as collateral. The token bounced after the reopening and is now holding roughly flat, as traders weigh how quickly it contained the risk.
crypto.meaning: The bounce reflects relief that Aave avoided losses, not a change in the broader downtrend. Lending protocols are exposed if stolen or volatile assets are used as collateral, so its handling of the incident matters for confidence.

outlook.bullCase: Continued calm and fresh deposits could carry it toward $150.
outlook.bearCase: Any bad debt revealed from the hack-related borrowing, or a wider crypto drop, could send it back to the $120s.
outlook.watch: Aave governance updates on the frozen assets; overall DeFi deposits.

sources.title: Bitcoin.com: Aave freezes lending across 16 networks after Binance hack
Cryptopolitan: Aave reopens all markets; nine assets stay at zero LTV

crypto.name: Morpho
crypto.move: Down 4.8% in 24h but up 7.7% this week, at about $2.26 (down 13.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Morpho, a DeFi (decentralized finance) lending network where users lend and borrow crypto without a bank, rose about 10% this week alongside Aave as lending tokens bounced after the hack-driven sell-off, but is giving back some of that gain on Sunday, down about 5% in 24 hours. We found no single new announcement behind the move in major outlets, so it looks like short-term traders rotating back into the lending sector.
crypto.meaning: Lending tokens are recovering because the Binance hack did not spread into DeFi lending losses, but a quick jump with no clear news can reverse just as fast. It remains a higher-risk, smaller asset than bitcoin or ether.

outlook.bullCase: If DeFi lending activity keeps recovering and the broader market steadies, it could push toward $2.50.
outlook.bearCase: If the bounce fades with no news to support it, it could slip back toward $2.15–$2.20, roughly where it traded a week ago.
outlook.watch: Deposits on Morpho and Aave; whether the move holds above $2.20 support; bitcoin's direction.

sources.title: CoinGecko: Morpho price and market data

crypto.name: Lighter
crypto.move: Up 7.1% in 24h and flat this week, at about $3.21 (down 12.4% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Lighter runs a perpetual-futures exchange (a venue for leveraged bets on crypto prices that never expire). Its token jumped about 20% on Oct. 22 after the team said it plans to seek a U.S. CFTC licence (the regulator for futures) and is weighing access through Robinhood, then gave much of that back in the hack-driven sell-off. It is leading Sunday's altcoin gainers, up about 10%, and sits near the top of CoinGecko's trending list, on more than $100 million of trading volume, but we found no new announcement behind the rebound in major outlets, so it looks like traders rotating back into exchange tokens after HYPE's strong week.
crypto.meaning: LIT is still down about 13% over 30 days, so Sunday's jump only repairs part of the damage. Its value depends heavily on the U.S. licence plan actually moving forward, and small-cap exchange tokens can give back gains as quickly as they make them.

outlook.bullCase: Concrete progress on the CFTC filing or a Robinhood listing, plus a calmer market, could push it back toward the $3.50–$4 range it traded in earlier this month.
outlook.bearCase: If the bounce fades with no news behind it, or bitcoin breaks below $76,000, LIT could slip back below $2.75.
outlook.watch: Any CFTC filing announcement; Robinhood listing news; whether it holds above about $3; bitcoin's direction.

sources.title: The Crypto Times: LIT jumps 20% as Lighter weighs U.S. licence and Robinhood access

crypto.name: Zcash
crypto.move: Down 4.7% in 24h but up 1.2% this week, at about $1,226 (down 9.9% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Traders are positioning ahead of Zcash's NU7 network upgrade, targeted for Nov. 5, which cuts the target time between blocks from 75 seconds to 25 seconds for faster payments. The privacy coin has been one of the strongest performers of the year.
crypto.meaning: Upgrades often bring a 'buy the rumour, sell the news' pattern: prices can rise into the event and fall after it. Expect sharp swings around Nov. 5.

outlook.bullCase: A smooth upgrade and continued interest in privacy coins could push it toward recent highs around $1,500.
outlook.bearCase: A delay, technical problem or profit-taking after the upgrade could pull it back toward $1,000 support.
outlook.watch: NU7 activation on Nov. 5; any delay announcement.

sources.title: Pluang: Zcash sets NU7 mainnet upgrade target of Nov. 5

crypto.name: Bitway
crypto.move: Down 2.3% in 24h and down 34.0% this week, at about $1.08 (down 23.8% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Bitway is down almost 60% from its Oct. 14 record of $2.77 as traders sell ahead of a token unlock of about 101.6 million BTW (roughly 1% of total supply) on Nov. 2 (Monday). Sources disagree on whether those tokens go to community pools or to early investors, who may be more likely to sell.
crypto.meaning: An unlock adds new tokens to the market; past Bitway unlocks were followed by an average drop of about 7% over two weeks, per CryptoTicker. Much of that risk may already be priced in after this week's slide, but volatility will stay extreme.

outlook.bullCase: If the unlocked tokens are not sold and buyers return, a rebound toward $1.50 is possible.
outlook.bearCase: If recipients sell into thin trading, it could slide toward $1.00 or below.
outlook.watch: The Nov. 2 unlock and on-chain transfers to exchanges.

crypto.name: Stacks
crypto.move: Down 4.1% in 24h but up 7.1% this week, at about $0.3223 (down 11.1% over 30 days)
crypto.why: Stacks, a network that adds smart contracts on top of bitcoin, has bounced sharply from recent lows. We found no single clear news catalyst in major outlets; the move looks driven by short-term traders.
crypto.meaning: Moves without a clear cause can reverse just as fast. It remains well below where it traded a month ago.

outlook.bullCase: Holding above $0.30 and a bitcoin recovery could extend the bounce toward $0.40.
outlook.bearCase: If the bounce fades, a return to the $0.27–$0.28 area is likely.
outlook.watch: Whether it holds $0.30; bitcoin's trend.

stocks.name: S&P 500
stocks.move: Down 1.8% Friday to about 7,580, and down 0.6% for the week; 3.4% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Friday was the worst day since June, led by tech after Intel's dismal outlook, Amazon's earnings miss and Alphabet's capex-heavy quarter. Rising expectations of a December Fed hike also weighed.
stocks.meaning: The index is still up about 11% this year, so this is a pullback, not a crash. But the market's biggest companies are now being punished for spending heavily on AI.

outlook.bullCase: Solid Apple results Monday and a calm midterm outcome could steady the index back toward 7,700–7,750.
outlook.bearCase: Another round of disappointing tech earnings or a strong jobs report that locks in a Fed hike could push it toward 7,400.
outlook.watch: Apple (Nov. 2), AMD (Nov. 3), midterms (Nov. 3), jobs report (Nov. 6).

stocks.name: Nasdaq Composite
stocks.move: Down 2.9% Friday to about 25,437, and down 2.0% for the week; 8.2% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Chipmakers led the drop: Intel fell 28.6%, AMD about 11%, Broadcom 5.5% and Nvidia 4.2%. The Nasdaq posted its worst month since March 2025.
stocks.meaning: Tech-heavy portfolios are most exposed to the AI-spending debate. Expect large daily moves while key tech earnings arrive.

outlook.bullCase: Strong AMD and Palantir results could spark a relief bounce toward 26,000.
outlook.bearCase: If those results disappoint, a further slide toward 24,500 is plausible.
outlook.watch: AMD and Palantir earnings; chip-stock reaction; 10-year yield near 5%.

stocks.name: S&P/TSX Composite
stocks.move: Down 1.7% Friday to about 35,620, and down 0.5% for the week; 3.9% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: Materials stocks fell 4.8% as gold sank to a one-year low and tech dropped 3%, while energy rose 1.7% with oil. Weak Canadian data also hurt: preliminary figures show GDP fell 0.1% in September.
stocks.meaning: The TSX is still up about 12% this year. Its mix of energy and miners means oil helps while gold hurts; rising Bank of Canada rates are a headwind for banks and real estate.

outlook.bullCase: Firm oil and a gold rebound could lift it back toward 36,200.
outlook.bearCase: Further gold weakness and more rate-hike talk could push it toward 35,000.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.move: Down 12.6% Thursday and 1.4% Friday, to about $279.84 (down 11.7% for the week)
stocks.why: Alphabet missed revenue and profit estimates while spending $51.4 billion on capital projects in the quarter, more than double a year earlier. Google Cloud revenue doubled, but search growth slowed to 12%, raising worries that AI chat tools are pressuring ad revenue. It was the stock's biggest one-day drop since its 2004 listing, per Stock Titan.
stocks.meaning: Investors are now weighing heavy spending against slowing growth in the core search business. The stock sits near its 52-week low of $270.70.

outlook.bullCase: Signs that cloud growth will pay for capex, or a broader tech rebound, could lift it back toward $300.
outlook.bearCase: A break below the $270 low would suggest more selling.
outlook.watch: The $270 support level; analyst revisions; the broader tech mood.

sources.title: Stock Titan: Alphabet misses forecasts, stock falls 12.6%

stocks.name: Intel
stocks.move: Down 28.6% Friday to about $65 (as of Friday's close, from news reports)
stocks.why: Intel guided fourth-quarter revenue to $15–16 billion, about 9% below expectations at the midpoint, with lower profit margins, because PC demand is weak even though data-centre and AI revenue grew 78%. It was the stock's worst day since 1974. It had risen about 250% this year before the drop.
stocks.meaning: After such a big run, the stock had little room for disappointment. Intel's drop also pulled down other chipmakers.

outlook.bullCase: If buyers see the PC slump as temporary, a partial rebound is possible; Morgan Stanley targets $75.
outlook.bearCase: More analyst cuts or wider chip weakness could push it lower.
outlook.watch: Analyst target changes; AMD's results Nov. 3.

sources.title: Stock Titan: Tech stocks fall as Intel has worst day in decades

stocks.name: AMD
stocks.move: Down 10.9% Friday to about $504.80 (down 2.3% for the week); 23% below its 52-week high
stocks.why: AMD fell with the chip sector after Intel's warning about weak PC demand, a market where AMD also sells processors. It reports its own results Tuesday after the close.
stocks.meaning: Tuesday's report is the key test. Expect a big move either way.

outlook.bullCase: Strong data-centre and AI chip numbers could recover much of Friday's drop, back above $550.
outlook.bearCase: A soft PC outlook like Intel's could push it toward $450.
outlook.watch: AMD earnings (Nov. 3, after close).

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.move: Down 1.4% Friday to about $240.35 (down 3.1% for the week)
stocks.why: Amazon's quarterly sales rose 12% to $201.9 billion and its AWS cloud unit grew 39%, but profit missed estimates and free cash flow over the past year was negative $42.4 billion because of AI spending. Shares fell as much as 7% before recovering most of the loss.
stocks.meaning: The quick recovery shows investors still value AWS growth, but spending is eating into the cash returned to shareholders.

outlook.bullCase: Continued strong AWS demand could lift it back toward $255.

stocks.meaning: Coinbase acts like a leveraged bet on crypto trading activity. A rival's troubles can draw customers, but weak sentiment is weighing for now.

newCoins.name: Lisk
newCoins.what: An older blockchain project whose original chain was scheduled to shut down permanently on Oct. 31, 2026, with holders required to migrate tokens to Ethereum.
newCoins.why: It jumped about 54% in 24 hours on Saturday and trended on CoinGecko as the Oct. 31 migration deadline arrived; earlier spikes were driven by migration-related trading rather than new products.
newCoins.redFlags: Tokens not migrated in time become unrecoverable; Binance put a monitoring tag on LSK in July; deadline-driven spikes often reverse.

sources.title: InteractiveCrypto: Lisk forces holders to migrate by Oct. 31

newCoins.name: Pearl
newCoins.what: A new blockchain launched in April 2026 that claims its mining also does useful AI computing; all coins come from mining, with no team or investor allocation.
newCoins.why: It rose about sevenfold between August and mid-October and is now ranked about 99th by market value (roughly $558 million, near $1.52 per coin). It is up about 34% over 30 days but down about 19% this week, and it is trending on CoinGecko, up about 4% in 24 hours.
newCoins.redFlags: A researcher showed miners can earn rewards without doing AI work; about 1 million new coins are mined daily, nearly doubling supply over a year; it trades on few exchanges with thin liquidity.

sources.title: Parameter: PRL surges sevenfold despite code controversy

newCoins.name: Kinetiq
newCoins.what: A liquid staking project on Hyperliquid: users lock up HYPE tokens to help secure the network and get a tradable receipt token back, so their HYPE keeps earning rewards while staying usable. KNTQ is its governance token.
newCoins.why: It is trending on CoinGecko at about $0.57 (market value near $182 million), up about 6% in 24 hours. It has been moving with HYPE, which jumped this week on the ICE (New York Stock Exchange owner) tie-up, and set a record near $0.50 on Oct. 29 before rising further.
newCoins.redFlags: Price closely tied to a single ecosystem (Hyperliquid); a young token with future unlocks likely; a large HYPE unlock on Nov. 6 could hit the whole ecosystem; thinner trading than major coins.

sources.title: KuCoin News: KNTQ passes $0.50
CoinGecko: Kinetiq

newCoins.name: Quantus
newCoins.what: A new blockchain built to resist future quantum computers, which could one day break the cryptography that protects today's coins. Its QTC token launched for trading on NEAR's near.com and NEAR Intents in early October.
newCoins.why: It trended on CoinGecko this week at about $73 per token, though its total market value was only about $23 million because very few tokens are in circulation; reports say its October rally was driven by that small float as much as by the quantum-safety story.
newCoins.redFlags: Very small circulating supply, so prices can swing wildly and more tokens may unlock later; thin trading on few venues; a young network with an unproven product.
